pagina.entradilla: On the road to Seville, along the Vía de la Plata, where the foothills of the Sierra Morena begin. The town where Francisco de Zurbarán was born.
pagina.descripcion: History, heritage, festivals and food of Fuente de Cantos (Badajoz, Spain).

historia: The hills of Los Castillejos, next to the town, were inhabited from the Neolithic until Roman times. The area was a compulsory crossing between Mérida and the Guadalquivir valley.

The name of Fuente de Cantos appears with the Christian conquest, around 1240. The first document in the municipal archive dates from 1293. The town belonged to the Commandery of Montemolín of the Order of Santiago, then it was a royal town, and in the 19th century it was the head of a judicial district.

The painter Francisco de Zurbarán was born here: he was baptised in the parish church on 7 November 1598. None of his more than 600 catalogued works is kept in the town today, but his birthplace can be visited.

The municipality covers 251.8 km² and the town stands at 582 metres above sea level, among vineyards, olive groves, dehesa (open oak pasture) and wheat fields. It belongs to the Tentudía region and to the judicial district of Zafra.

Parroquia de Nuestra Señora de la Granad.nombre: Parish church of Nuestra Señora de la Granada
Parroquia de Nuestra Señora de la Granad.texto: A Bien de Interés Cultural (listed heritage site). It keeps the 16th-century baptismal font in which Zurbarán was baptised.
Parroquia de Nuestra Señora de la Granad.alt: Façade of the parish church with the clock tower, the stone base of the old tower and storks' nests

Casa natal de Zurbarán.texto: On Calle Águilas. Restored in 2014, with six rooms about the painter and his time.
Casa natal de Zurbarán.alt: Whitewashed façade with a wooden gate, the number 37 and two plaques

Santuario de la Hermosa.nombre: Shrine of the Hermosa (Santuario de la Hermosa)
Santuario de la Hermosa.texto: The shrine of the patron saint, from the 15th century, remodelled in the 18th.
Santuario de la Hermosa.alt: A street of white houses ending at the white façade of the shrine, with its bell gable

Casa Consistorial.texto: In the Plaza de la Constitución, among palm trees.
Casa Consistorial.alt: White façade of the Town Hall with a balcony and flags, among palm trees

Ermita de San Juan de Letrán.nombre: Chapel of San Juan de Letrán
Ermita de San Juan de Letrán.texto: It began as a hospital in 1515. It is one of the two chapels that can be visited.
Ermita de San Juan de Letrán.alt: Whitewashed chapel with its side chapel and the gated door, under a blue sky

Convento de San Diego.texto: Franciscan, with the church finished in 1624. Today it hosts cultural events.
Convento de San Diego.alt: Ochre façade of the former convent among trees

Ermita de San Isidro.texto: In the meadow of the pilgrimage (romería), on the outskirts.
Ermita de San Isidro.alt: White chapel with a lantern and a rider with his rearing horse in front

Monumento a Zurbarán.texto: The painter, in bronze and with his palette, in the park that bears his name.
Monumento a Zurbarán.alt: Bronze statue of Zurbarán with the palette, on a granite pedestal

Los Castillejos.texto: An archaeological site with Chalcolithic and Iron Age walls, next to the road to Fregenal.
Los Castillejos.alt: Dry-stone wall of the archaeological site

Parroquia de Nuestra Señora de la Granad.nombre: Parish church of Nuestra Señora de la Granada
Parroquia de Nuestra Señora de la Granad.detalle: Bien de Interés Cultural since 1990. The base of the old tower is from the 15th century, the sacristy from the 16th and the nave from the 18th. It keeps the Virgen de la Granada, from the 16th century, an image of San Roque, the patron saint, and the marble baptismal font in which Zurbarán was baptised.

Santuario de Nuestra Señora de la Hermos.nombre: Shrine of Nuestra Señora de la Hermosa
Santuario de Nuestra Señora de la Hermos.detalle: 15th century, remodelled in the 18th. Inside, an American canvas of the Cristo de la Encina and «La Aparecida», a Gothic carving of the 14th century.

Convento de las Carmelitas Descalzas.nombre: Convent of the Discalced Carmelites (Convento de las Carmelitas Descalzas)
Convento de las Carmelitas Descalzas.detalle: Founded in 1649 by Juan de Escobar del Corro. Main altarpiece by Juan Martínez de Vargas (1675).

Convento de San Diego.detalle: Franciscan. The church was finished in 1624 and the convent was suppressed in 1835. It keeps the chapel of the Corazón de Jesús.

Ermita de San Juan de Letrán.nombre: Chapel of San Juan de Letrán
Ermita de San Juan de Letrán.detalle: On Calle Almenas. It began as a hospital in 1515.

Ermita de la Aurora.detalle: No longer used for worship. It keeps its Baroque bell gable.

Ermita de San Isidro.detalle: In the meadow where the pilgrimage (romería) is held.

Casa de los Panea y Plaza de Zurbarán.nombre: Casa de los Panea and Plaza de Zurbarán
Casa de los Panea y Plaza de Zurbarán.detalle: The Casa de los Panea, known as «Casa Perrete», and the Modernist square with the monument to the Corazón de Jesús.

Antigua fábrica harinera.detalle: From the early 20th century, on Calle Real. A protected building.

Yacimiento de Los Castillejos I y II.nombre: Archaeological site of Los Castillejos I and II
Yacimiento de Los Castillejos I y II.detalle: From the Neolithic to Roman times, with a Chalcolithic wall and an Iron Age wall.

Colonias de cernícalo primilla.detalle: The built-up area is a Special Protection Area for Birds (ZEPA).

Artesanía campera.detalle: Wooden pots and spoons, horn spoons, country leather bottles (botas camperas) and shepherds' huts (chozos).

Carnaval.cuando: February or March, with the comparsas (carnival groups) in the Teatro Municipal

Fiesta de la Chanfaina.cuando: Last weekend of April. A Festival of Tourist Interest of Extremadura

Romería de San Isidro.cuando: 15 May. A Festival of Tourist Interest of Extremadura

Fiesta de San Juan.nombre: San Juan festival (Fiesta de San Juan)
Fiesta de San Juan.cuando: The Saturday closest to 24 June, in the San Juan quarter

Fiestas del Jubileo y San Roque.nombre: Jubileo festivals and San Roque (Fiestas del Jubileo y San Roque)
Fiestas del Jubileo y San Roque.cuando: 14 to 18 August; San Roque, the patron saint, on the 16th

platos: Chanfaina de cordero (lamb stew, the town's signature dish)
Productos del cerdo ibérico (Iberian pork products)
pueblo.gastronomia_alt: A cauldron of chanfaina boiling over the embers of a bonfire

Francisco de Zurbarán.texto: Painter of the Spanish Golden Age. Baptised in the parish church of Fuente de Cantos, he trained in Seville and settled in Llerena in 1617.

Nicolás Megía.texto: Painter. Medal in 1890 for «La defensa de Zaragoza». A street, a park and the nursery school bear his name.

Juan de Escobar del Corro.texto: In 1649 he founded the college that gave rise to the convent of the Discalced Carmelites.

Vía de la Plata: Fuente de Cantos - Zafr.resumen: 24 km among olive groves and cereal fields, with villages with services at 6 and 20 km.

Fuente El Lobo.resumen: 17 km, low difficulty. From the Plaza de Colón along La Senda to the spring; back along the Bienvenida track.

La Cañada Real - La Senda.resumen: 14 km, medium difficulty. Past the chapel of San Juan and along the Cañada Real (drove road) to the Cabeza Gorda hill.

Las Zorrillas.resumen: 17 km, medium difficulty. Along the Monesterio track and the vereda de los Carboneros (drove road).

Cortijo Palominos.resumen: 22 km, medium difficulty. Along the Monesterio track to Las Zorrillas; back along the Camino de Santiago.

Las Horneras.resumen: 23 km, medium difficulty. Along the vereda de los Carboneros (drove road); back along the Bienvenida track.

Las Talliscas - Bodión - El Risco.resumen: 20 km, medium difficulty. Along the Valencia del Ventoso track to the river Bodión.

La Argamasa.resumen: 33 km, medium difficulty. Along the Camino de Santiago and Calzadilla; back along the Vía de la Plata.
